To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the way that the wind energy is priced in the market impacts premiums and that the expansion of wind energy capacity reduces market power.
The integration of wind power into electricity markets can increase market power and premiums in day ahead markets.
the integration of wind power capacity into electricity markets has a significant impact on the efficiency of the electricity market and the level of premiums.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the impact of the expansion of wind power capacity in deregulated electricity markets.
the impact of the integration of intermittent renewable energy on electricity market efficiency and the role of pricing mechanisms in the presence of wind power.
the impact of expansion of wind power capacity on day ahead premiums in the electricity market.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expansion of wind power capacity in the presence of market power is detrimental for the efficiency of electricity markets.
pricing wind energy via a FIT arrangement is the preferred approach.

the integration of wind power capacity into the electricity market is a positive development, as it reduces market power and increases market efficiency, but only if the wind energy is priced via a market independent FIT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expansion of wind power capacity and pricing methods impact the efficiency of deregulated electricity markets in a significant manner.
wind energy is a double edged sword.

the expansion of wind power capacity in the presence of wind energy pricing in the market increases the ability of firms to extract oversized day-ahead premiums, while in the case that wind energy is not allowed to be traded in the market, the expansion of wind capacity leads to a decrease in market power and thus in premiums.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expansion of wind energy capacity and the pricing mechanism used to accommodate its variability are key factors in shaping the performance of electricity markets.
the integration of wind power into the electricity system can be beneficial to the market as a whole if wind energy is priced appropriately.
the integration of wind power capacity has an ambiguous impact on the efficiency of electricity markets.
